items.title: ECOWAS bank announces its 2027 Investment Forum
items.summary: The ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development will host its Investment Forum on 7 and 8 April 2027, bringing together investors, development banks, policymakers and private-sector leaders.

vocab.eg: Our bank will host the forum in April.
We will brief all stakeholders on Monday.
Capital inflows rose in the third quarter.

items.title: BOAD briefs Ivorian companies on how to borrow from it
items.summary: On 1 October in Abidjan, the West African Development Bank explained to local firms how they can access its financing.

vocab.eg: Small firms struggle to access financing.

items.title: Côte d’Ivoire’s US$206 billion investment plan
items.summary: The 2026–2030 National Development Plan envisages up to US$206 billion in investment, with about 70 percent expected to come from the private sector.

vocab.eg: The plan envisages new roads and ports.
The private sector will fund most projects.
Sales are expected to rise next year.

items.title: Côte d’Ivoire reshapes its cocoa model to capture more value
items.summary: The country is adjusting how it manages cocoa, aiming to protect its markets and keep more of the value of its crop at home.

vocab.eg: We want to capture more value in the chain.
The reform will reshape the sector.

items.title: Morocco’s Attijariwafa to buy Société Générale’s Ghana business
items.summary: Attijariwafa is acquiring Société Générale’s operations in Ghana, another sign of African banks expanding across borders.

vocab.eg: The group plans to acquire a local bank.
We want to expand into West Africa.

items.title: Africa’s financial power map is changing
items.summary: Kenya and Egypt now place more banks in the global top 500 than Nigeria and South Africa, a sign that the continent’s banking centres of gravity are shifting.

vocab.eg: The bank moved up in the ranking.
The focus is shifting to digital banking.
Sales overtook last year’s total in June.
